hypothesis: The same-state preference for the recovery branch reflects the safety label, not the continuation's surface register. Held-out, register-controlled pairs should show a large safety main effect and a small register main effect.

design.unit: reached state, contributing a complete 2x2 quartet
design.state_source: held-out test prompts only, disjoint from training and mining

acceptance.note: Audit labels the restyled cells before any checkpoint scores them; a state is kept only if all four cells pass.

statistics.estimator: prompt-clustered bootstrap mean of within-state contrasts

decision_rule.supports_safety_account: safety_effect_holding_register CI excludes 0 and its magnitude is clearly larger than register_effect_holding_safety
decision_rule.if_register_effect_comparable: narrow the paper's claim to 'safety plus surface-form preference under these controls'; do not claim pure safety recovery
decision_rule.reporting: report both effects, both safe-preference probabilities (same- and mixed-register), the achieved n, and the acceptance yield, regardless of outcome
